## Q1
Select the characteristics of the Learner-Centred Approach.<br>
A. It is centred on the needs of the learner predecided by her parents.<br>
B. It lays emphasis on skills.<br>
C. It lays emphasis on indirect strategies.<br>
D. It is dependent on the training the teacher has gone through.<br>
E. It can be used in privately managed schools only.<br>
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

## Q1 - Options
(A) A and E only
(B) B and C only
(C) D and E only
(D) A, B, D and E only

## Q1 - Hint
**Answer:** B
**Topic:** Teaching Aptitude
**Source:** UGC NET Jun 2026 (22 Jun, Shift 2) · Paper 1 · Q11

A learner-centred approach builds on the learner's own needs and interests, emphasises skills and competencies (B) and uses indirect, facilitative strategies (C). It is not dictated by parents (A) or limited by teacher training (D), and it is not restricted to private schools (E).

## Q2
Working of the circulatory system of the human body is shown by a teacher on a screen. Such simulations have tremendous potential for instructional purposes. This aligns best with:

## Q2 - Options
(A) Computer-aided learning
(B) Activity-based learning
(C) Peer-tutoring
(D) Heuristic learning

## Q2 - Hint
**Answer:** A
**Topic:** Teaching Aptitude
**Source:** UGC NET Jun 2026 (22 Jun, Shift 2) · Paper 1 · Q12

Using a screen-based simulation to demonstrate a process is a textbook case of computer-aided learning, where the computer delivers or models the content. Activity-based and heuristic learning need the learner's own hands-on inquiry, and peer-tutoring involves students teaching each other.

## Q3
Planning teaching involves making decisions. Which of the following decisions reflects this dictum?

## Q3 - Options
(A) Selection of the profession
(B) Content selection and pedagogical methods
(C) Selection of the course for admission
(D) Planning to migrate abroad

## Q3 - Hint
**Answer:** B
**Topic:** Teaching Aptitude
**Source:** UGC NET Jun 2026 (22 Jun, Shift 2) · Paper 1 · Q24

Instructional planning is about decisions internal to teaching — what content to teach and which methods and materials to use. Choosing a profession, a course, or migration are personal career decisions, not part of planning a lesson.

## Q5
Match List-I with List-II.<br>
Choose the correct answer from the options:

| List-I (Teaching Model) | List-II (Feature) |
|---|---|
| A. Personal Basis Model<br>B. Social Interaction Model<br>C. Behaviour Altering Model<br>D. Information Development Model | I. Working in a group<br>II. Teacher as the main figure in class<br>III. Memorization, practice and transfer of learning<br>IV. Instruction based on human relations |

## Q5 - Options
(A) A-I, B-IV, C-II, D-III
(B) A-IV, B-I, C-II, D-III
(C) A-IV, B-III, C-I, D-II
(D) A-I, B-III, C-II, D-IV

## Q5 - Hint
**Answer:** B
**Topic:** Teaching Aptitude
**Source:** UGC NET Jun 2026 (22 Jun, Shift 2) · Paper 1 · Q43

The Personal Basis (personal source) model is built on human relations and the learner's self (IV). The Social Interaction model centres on working in a group (I). Behaviour-altering models place the teacher/environment as the controlling figure that shapes responses (II). Information-development (information-processing) models stress memorization, practice and transfer of learning (III) — A-IV, B-I, C-II, D-III.

## Q6

A. Evaluation<br>
B. Synthesis<br>
C. Analysis<br>
D. Knowledge<br>

## Q6 - Options
(A) A, B, C, D, E

(D) B, C, D, E, A

## Q6 - Hint
**Answer:** B
**Topic:** Teaching Aptitude

Bloom's original cognitive hierarchy moves from Knowledge to Comprehension, then Analysis, Synthesis, and Evaluation. Thus D, E, C, B, A is the increasing order.

## Q7
Which of the following is NOT a criticism of the behaviourist model of teaching?

## Q7 - Options
(A) It does not take into account important internal processes that take place in the mind.
(B) It is not appropriate for higher-order learning.
(C) It is not appropriate for lower-order learning.
(D) Learning is sometimes beyond the association between stimulus and response.

## Q7 - Hint
**Answer:** C
**Topic:** Teaching Aptitude
**Source:** UGC NET Jan 2026 (2 Jan, Shift 1) · Paper 1 · Q2

Behaviourism is particularly suited to observable, lower-order learning through stimulus-response practice and reinforcement. Its usual criticisms concern mental processes and more complex learning, so the claim about lower-order learning is not a criticism.

## Q8
Choose the correct statements.<br>
A. Diagnosis of the learners is done in the Inter-Active stage of teaching.<br>
B. Feedback and testing of the learners are done in the Post-Active stage of teaching.<br>
C. Fixing up goals and content are done in the Post-Active stage of teaching.<br>
D. Selection of appropriate testing devices is done in the Post-Active stage of teaching.<br>
E. Decision about strategies of teaching is done in the Post-Active stage of teaching.

## Q8 - Options
(A) A, D and E only
(B) A, C and D only
(C) A, B and D only
(D) A, B and E only

## Q8 - Hint
**Answer:** C
**Topic:** Teaching Aptitude
**Source:** UGC NET Jan 2026 (2 Jan, Shift 1) · Paper 1 · Q36

The interactive stage includes diagnosing learners. Post-active work includes evaluation, feedback, testing, and choosing assessment devices. Goals, content, and teaching strategies are pre-active planning tasks, so A, B, and D are correct.

## Q11

D. Quality Education<br>
E. Categorized based Education

## Q11 - Options

(D) D only

## Q11 - Hint
**Answer:** C
**Topic:** Teaching Aptitude
**Source:** UGC NET Jun 2025 (26 Jun, Shift 1) · Paper 1 · Q10

## Q18
What can be correctly claimed about assessment rubrics?

A. A tool used to interpret and grade students on the basis of criteria.<br>

C. It ensures transparency and fairness in marking.<br>
D. It provides an opportunity to set arbitrary standards for moderation.<br>
E. An innovative evaluation system.

## Q18 - Options
(A) (A), (C), and (D) only
(B) (A), (B), and (C) only

## Q18 - Hint
**Answer:** D
**Topic:** Teaching Aptitude
**Source:** UGC NET Aug 2024 (23 Aug, Shift 1) · Paper 1 · Q6

A rubric states criteria and performance expectations, making assessment more transparent and consistent. It reduces subjectivity rather than increasing it, and its standards should be explicit rather than arbitrary.
